title: Signature Runtime Rosetta
description: Signature original — a compatibility layer that describes each runtime's operator semantics in one shared specification language, then generates the glue for cross-runtime moves automatically. Instead of hand-written converters per pair, every runtime implements the Rosetta spec once. New runtimes plug in by writing one adapter instead of N converters.

title: Signature Profile Synthesizer
description: Signature original — synthesizes TensorRT-style optimization profiles from observed production shapes instead of hand-picked ranges. The synthesizer clusters a week of shape logs and emits the minimal profile set covering 99.9 percent of traffic. Engines stop failing on unseen-but-ordinary shapes.

demo.code:
from collections import Counter
shapes = [4]*500 + [16]*300 + [32]*150 + [64]*49 + [128]
top = Counter(shapes).most_common(3)
covered = sum(c for _, c in top) / len(shapes)
print("top shapes:", top)
print("coverage: %.1f%%" % (100 * covered))

title: Signature Quantization Passport
description: Signature original — a sidecar file that travels with a quantized model recording the exact scales, zero points, and calibration data hash used. Any runtime importing the model reads the passport instead of guessing quantization parameters. Parity disputes become a diff of two passports instead of a debugging saga.
verdict: Ship the passport with the model

demo.code:
passport = {"scale": 0.02, "zero_point": 128, "calib_hash": "9f3a", "method": "minmax"}
print("passport:", passport)
print("importer applies scale", passport["scale"], "zp", passport["zero_point"], "-> no guessing")
_jah_schema = {'technique': 'Signature passport', 'runtime_a': 'Quantized model', 'runtime_b': 'Any runtime', 'compat_area': 'Quantization metadata', 'verdict': 'Ship the passport with the model', 'complexity': 'Low'}
print("technique:", _jah_schema["technique"])
assert set(_jah_schema) == set(['technique', 'runtime_a', 'runtime_b', 'compat_area', 'verdict', 'complexity']) and all(_jah_schema.values())
print("schema verified:", len(_jah_schema), "fields")

title: Signature Delegate Arbiter
description: Signature original — at startup the arbiter benchmarks every available delegate on the actual device with the actual model and picks the winner per subgraph. It re-arbitrates when the device changes, such as thermal throttling kicking in. Delegate choice becomes measured instead of configured.

demo.code:
import random
random.seed(3)
cands = {"gpu": 6.3, "npu": 4.1, "cpu": 28.0}
jitter = {k: v * random.uniform(0.95, 1.05) for k, v in cands.items()}
best = min(jitter, key=jitter.get)
print("measured:", {k: round(v, 2) for k, v in jitter.items()})
print("arbiter picks:", best)

title: Signature Opset Time Machine
description: Signature original — a downgrader that rewrites newer opset operators into equivalent sequences of older opset operators, so a model exported at opset 18 runs on a runtime pinned to opset 14. Each rewrite is verified numerically against the original. Legacy fleets keep running without runtime upgrades.

demo.code:
rewrites = {"gelu": ["erf", "mul", "add"], "layer_norm": ["sub", "div", "mul"]}
model_ops = ["gelu", "conv"]
needed = [o for o in model_ops if o in rewrites]
print("ops needing rewrite:", needed)
print("all rewritable:", all(o in rewrites for o in needed))

title: Signature Engine Foundry
description: Signature original — a build farm abstraction that compiles one source model into per-GPU-arch TensorRT engines in parallel and versions them as a set. The serving layer picks the engine matching the detected GPU at startup. Adding a new GPU generation means adding one foundry worker, not rewriting deployment.

demo.code:
archs = ["sm_75", "sm_80", "sm_90"]
engines = {a: "engine_%s.plan" % a for a in archs}
detected = "sm_80"
print("foundry built:", len(engines), "engines")
print("detected", detected, "-> load", engines[detected])

title: Signature Web Fallback Ladder
description: Signature original — for browser deployment the ladder tries WebGPU, then WASM SIMD, then WASM scalar, measuring which actually works on the visitor's device. The model ships once and the ladder picks the rung at runtime. Capability detection replaces user-agent sniffing.

demo.code:
rungs = ["webgpu", "wasm-simd", "wasm"]
available = {"webgpu": False, "wasm-simd": True, "wasm": True}
pick = next(r for r in rungs if available[r])
print("available:", available)
print("ladder picks:", pick)

title: Signature Parity Ledger
description: Signature original — records every cross-runtime numeric comparison as a ledger entry with inputs hash, tolerance, and verdict. Regressions are caught by replaying the ledger in CI. The ledger is the institutional memory of what parity means for each model.

demo.code:
ledger = [{"model": "m1", "tol": 1e-3, "verdict": "pass"}]
entry = {"model": "m1", "tol": 1e-3, "verdict": "pass"}
print("replay verdict:", "pass" if entry in ledger else "NEW - investigate")
_jah_schema = {'technique': 'Signature parity ledger', 'runtime_a': 'Runtime A', 'runtime_b': 'Runtime B', 'compat_area': 'Numeric parity', 'verdict': 'Ledger in CI', 'complexity': 'Medium'}
print("technique:", _jah_schema["technique"])
assert set(_jah_schema) == set(['technique', 'runtime_a', 'runtime_b', 'compat_area', 'verdict', 'complexity']) and all(_jah_schema.values())
print("schema verified:", len(_jah_schema), "fields")

title: Signature Thermal Governor
description: Signature original — monitors device temperature during mobile inference and migrates subgraphs between Neural Engine and GPU as thermal state changes. The governor keeps frame rates stable instead of letting the device throttle into stutter. Migration cost is weighed against the throttle penalty before each move.

demo.code:
temp, migrate_cost, throttle_penalty = 44.0, 30, 120
decision = "migrate to GPU" if throttle_penalty > migrate_cost and temp > 42 else "stay"
print("temp %.1fC -> %s" % (temp, decision))
_jah_schema = {'technique': 'Signature thermal gov', 'runtime_a': 'CoreML ANE', 'runtime_b': 'CoreML GPU', 'compat_area': 'Thermal throttling', 'verdict': 'Migrate on thermals', 'complexity': 'High'}
print("technique:", _jah_schema["technique"])
assert set(_jah_schema) == set(['technique', 'runtime_a', 'runtime_b', 'compat_area', 'verdict', 'complexity']) and all(_jah_schema.values())
print("schema verified:", len(_jah_schema), "fields")

title: Signature Input Ritual
description: Signature original — a preprocessing contract that hashes the exact preprocessing pipeline and bakes the hash into the model package. At runtime the app's preprocessing hash must match or inference refuses to run. Silent preprocessing mismatches, the most common parity bug, become loud immediate errors.

demo.code:
import hashlib
pipe = "resize256|center224|normalize(imagenet)"
h = hashlib.sha256(pipe.encode()).hexdigest()[:8]
print("pipeline hash:", h)
print("runtime check:", "PASS" if h == hashlib.sha256(pipe.encode()).hexdigest()[:8] else "FAIL")

title: Signature Provider Compass
description: Signature original — a decision procedure that picks the ONNX Runtime execution provider from hardware detection plus a 60-second benchmark, encoded as a repeatable script. The compass removes guesswork from provider selection and documents why each provider won. Rerunning the compass after driver updates catches regressions.

demo.code:
bench = {"cuda": 5.9, "tensorrt": 3.8, "cpu": 41.0}
winner = min(bench, key=bench.get)
print("60s benchmark:", bench)
print("compass pins:", winner)

title: Signature Flex Diet
description: Signature original — a rewriter that replaces Flex-delegate ops with sequences of builtin TFLite ops wherever a known equivalence exists, shrinking the binary back down. The diet is verified numerically op by op. Models keep their behavior and lose their megabytes.

demo.code:
equiv = {"gelu": ["erf_approx", "mul"], "mish": ["tanh", "mul"]}
model = ["gelu", "conv"]
diet = [equiv.get(o, [o]) for o in model]
print("after diet:", diet)
print("flex still needed:", any(o not in equiv and o not in ("conv",) for o in model if o in equiv) == False)

title: Signature KV-Cache Passport

title: Signature Edge Matchmaker
description: Signature original — matches models to edge runtimes by scoring operator coverage, precision support, and measured latency in one report. The matchmaker tries OpenVINO, TFLite, and ORT on the actual edge box and ranks them. Runtime choice becomes a benchmark result instead of a habit.

demo.code:
scores = {"openvino": 0.91, "tflite": 0.62, "ort": 0.78}
ranked = sorted(scores, key=scores.get, reverse=True)
print("scores:", scores)
print("ranking:", ranked)

title: Signature Shape Treaty
description: Signature original — a contract format where the model declares the exact shape ranges it was validated on, and the runtime refuses out-of-contract shapes with a clear error instead of silently misbehaving. The treaty travels with the model file. Shape bugs move from production incidents to deploy-time rejections.

title: Signature Thread Tuner
description: Signature original — autotunes ONNX Runtime session options by sweeping thread counts and arena settings against a latency target, then writes the winning config to a file the app loads. The tuner reruns when it detects new hardware. Free performance without touching the model.

demo.code:
sweep = {1: 38.2, 2: 21.0, 4: 12.4, 8: 11.8, 16: 12.9}
best = min(sweep, key=sweep.get)
print("thread sweep ms:", sweep)
print("tuner pins threads =", best)

title: Signature Version Vault
description: Signature original — pins the full runtime version matrix (runtime, drivers, converters) that a model was validated against, and CI re-validates parity whenever any component version changes. The vault makes 'it worked on my machine' impossible: the validated matrix is the deployable matrix.

title: Signature Unit Dialect
description: Signature original — a units-and-dtype annotation dialect that travels with tensors between runtimes, so a milliseconds-vs-seconds or fp16-vs-fp32 mismatch is caught at the boundary. The dialect is checked, not trusted. Boundary bugs become compile-time errors.

title: Signature Cold-Start Primer
description: Signature original — warms runtime sessions with representative inputs during app startup so the first real inference is as fast as the hundredth. The primer replays the shapes the treaty declares. Cold-start latency spikes disappear from user-visible metrics.

demo.code:
import time
cold, warm = 210.0, 8.4
print("cold first inference: %.1f ms" % cold)
print("after priming: %.1f ms" % warm)
print("user-visible spike removed: %.1fx" % (cold / warm))
